name: Public-sector contract prime/subcontract broker
one_liner: Bid on government contracts as the prime contractor, subcontract the delivery to an established local firm, and keep the margin.
customer: Government buyers (in the transcript, US federal agencies; the UK equivalent is public bodies posting on Contracts Finder and Find a Tender)
offer: Delivered services such as painting and facilities work, subcontracted to vetted local providers
how_it_makes_money: Spread between the subcontractor's price and the contract price. Example: a $41,000 sub cost billed at $52,000 gave $11,000 profit; a $700,000 sub cost billed at $962,000. Multi-year contracts can bring recurring income.
startup_cost: low ('You don't need any money', registration is free)
time_to_first_revenue: Weeks to months. The guest won the first contract they bid on, and that job made $11k profit in two weeks of delivery.
tools: UK Contracts Finder / Find a Tender
evidence: 'My subcontractor charged me $41,000 and I charged the government $52,000. So I made $11,000 profit in just a two week time period.' (xrU6tVo-qME)
'My sub-contractor charged me $700,000 and I was able to charge the government $962,000.' (xrU6tVo-qME)
Claims about an hour a month to maintain existing contracts (xrU6tVo-qME)
risks: Set-aside advantages in the US ('government is required to spend money with us') may not carry over to the UK
Liability for subcontractor non-performance sits with the prime
Payment terms may require cash float to pay the sub
Claims of 'easy' and 'an hour a month' are likely survivorship bias
UK frameworks and qualification requirements (insurance, accreditations) add friction

name: Niche hobby course + paid membership
one_liner: Become the go-to online resource for a narrow hobby or husbandry niche and sell courses plus a recurring paid community.
customer: Hobbyists in a specific niche (e.g., goat owners and homesteaders)
offer: Online courses, a paid membership community, a book, and a podcast/YouTube as the top of the funnel
how_it_makes_money: Course sales during cart-open launches plus recurring membership fees. Six-figure business; about 75% of buyers purchased as soon as the cart opened. Exact prices are not stated.
time_to_first_revenue: Unknown. It took years of content building (blog since the 2000s, goats focus for 7-8 years).
evidence: 'Deborah runs a six figure online business in an unlikely niche' (yBj1SM4MrIQ)
'probably 75% of people bought as soon as the card opened' (yBj1SM4MrIQ)
'helped thousands of customers through her online courses and... a thriving paid membership community' (yBj1SM4MrIQ)
risks: Slow audience build; early income was below fast-food wages
Needs real expertise or credibility in the niche
Success depends on picking a niche with passionate, paying hobbyists
Founder fit only works if the founder has a niche they know well (a Portuguese or UK-specific angle or language could be a differentiator)

name: Coin-op machine placement in host venues
one_liner: Buy used coin-operated machines cheaply and place them in high-traffic venues like laundromats, grocery stores and bars on a revenue split.
customer: Members of the public using the machines; venue owners get a cut
offer: Placed machines. The machine type in the laundromat case is not specified in the digest; the other examples include grocery store machines and bar pool tables.
how_it_makes_money: Per-use machine revenue split with the host venue. A grocery store machine grosses $600-$2,400 a month before the store's split. The laundromat operator's first $600 machine paid back in 4 months, and the business now clears over $30k a month.
startup_cost: low ($600 for the first used machine; the other video's category is 'under about $10,000')
time_to_first_revenue: Immediate once placed; payback about 4 months in the case cited
evidence: 'bought his first machine off of a Facebook marketplace listing for $600... made back his money in just four months... clearing over $30,000 a month' (zlr9A2zQtUU)
'One machine grosses $600 to $2,400 a month before the stores split. First move, walk into one local grocery store and ask the store manager' (xlRvc4vgPAs)
risks: Needs physical servicing, collections and repairs, so it is not async
The $30k/month figure is a single outlier case
Venue may terminate the placement
Theft and vandalism
UK gaming/amusement licensing may apply depending on machine type

name: Land/asset lease brokering (towers, slips, wall space)
one_liner: Help landowners and property owners monetise idle assets such as ground leases for towers, boat slips and blank walls by researching rates and negotiating deals.
customer: Landowners and property owners with idle assets; the payer is telecom firms, boaters or advertisers
offer: Lease research and negotiation for underused assets, or leasing your own assets
how_it_makes_money: Monthly lease income. National ground leases run roughly $500-$2,500 a month (average about $900-$1,300). A broker model would take a commission, but that is not stated in the transcript.
startup_cost: low (first moves are free phone calls) if brokering; high if acquiring land
evidence: 'National ground leases run roughly $500 to $2,500 a month with the industry database average sitting around 900 to $1,300' (xlRvc4vgPAs)
Weak evidence for a broker model; the transcript frames these as owner income, listicle style
